frontend.prompt:
Shared contract facts (repeat of every explicit fact from requirement):
1) Create and update responses for an entry gain a new response field named "display_title".  
2) display_title is computed by this rule: measure the full title by Unicode code points; if length ≤ 30 code points return the full title unchanged; otherwise take the first 30 code points and append an ellipsis character (U+2026 '…').  
3) After a successful create or update, the frontend must immediately use response.display_title for user feedback; the canonical stored field "title" must continue to contain the full value.  
4) Affected layers: api_contract, frontend_pages, backend_services.  
5) List and detail API responses MUST NOT add display_title; list and detail pages should continue to display titles by applying the rule in (2) on the frontend (i.e., compute client-side for list/detail).  
6) Requests MUST NOT include display_title; if a request contains display_title the server must reject it with HTTP 422.  
7) Server-side logs related to the create/update second-step must be retained (logs are preserved).  
8) Implementation instructions only; do not invent or assume any historical or unspecified contract details; do not make decisions about unspecified items (e.g., exact endpoint paths, schema filenames) — those must be filled from the existing API contract.

Front-end implementation instructions (apply to frontend_pages and api_contract consumer behavior):
A. API contract adjustments (frontend role):
   - Do not modify API definitions of list or detail responses. They must remain unchanged. Document in the local API client that list/detail responses do NOT include display_title.  
   - For create and update responses, prepare the frontend API client to accept an additional optional response field display_title on the entry create/update success body. Do NOT attempt to add display_title to request payloads. (Do not change server schema files here; only adapt client parsing to accept the new response field.)

B. Runtime behavior changes:
   1) Create/Update flows:
      - After sending the create or update request, parse the response body and if response.display_title is present, use it immediately in all UI feedback (confirmation banners, inline success text, editing previews, etc.).  
      - Continue to send only the canonical "title" field in requests. Under no circumstances include display_title in outgoing requests. Add a guard/validation in the client request builder that removes any display_title if accidentally present or raises an error prior to sending.  
   2) List and Detail pages:
      - Continue to receive titles from list/detail APIs without display_title. For rendering list/detail views, compute display_title client-side using rule (2) above (measure by Unicode code points; if >30 code points, truncate to first 30 code points and append U+2026). Use the same truncation algorithm as used server-side to ensure visual parity.  

C. Input/output validation & safety:
   - Add a pre-send unit check in the network layer that asserts outgoing request bodies do not contain display_title. If found, either strip it and log a development-time error or block the request and surface an error in dev/staging. This prevents accidental contract violations.  

D. Tests / acceptance criteria for frontend:
   - Unit tests for the truncate-by-codepoints function with cases: lengths 0, 1, 29, 30, 31, multi-code-point characters (e.g., emoji, combining marks). Assert the appended ellipsis is U+2026 when truncated.  
   - Integration/QA tests for create/update: simulate a create/update response that includes display_title and verify the UI immediately shows the response.display_title value.  
   - Integration/QA tests for list/detail: verify that list/detail responses (which do not include display_title) are rendered by computing display_title client-side and that the computed value matches server behavior (use shared test vectors).  
   - Regression test: sending a request that includes display_title must not happen from the UI; test the pre-send guard.

E. Implementation notes and explicit omissions / open items for coordination:
   - Omission (frontend): Implementation must NOT attempt to implement server-side request validation or server logging — those are backend responsibilities.  
   - Omission (frontend): Do not change list/detail API schemas or add display_title to list/detail responses. If an API contract change is requested, coordinate with API contract owners.  
   - Required confirmation from API contract owners before coding: exact create/update endpoint names and the exact response JSON shape to update in the API client. Do not invent endpoint paths or response envelope structures; use the canonical API contract files in the repository.

Deliverables for frontend team:
   - Code changes in the API client to accept display_title in create/update responses.  
   - Client-side truncate-by-codepoints utility (shared across list/detail and any other UI).  
   - Pre-send guard that prevents sending display_title.  
   - Unit and integration tests listed above.  
   - A short PR description referencing the API contract change and requesting backend confirmation for the endpoint and schema used.

Back-end implementation instructions (apply to backend_services and api_contract provider changes):
A. API contract changes (server/provider responsibilities):
   - Modify the create and update response schema for the entry resource to include a new optional string field display_title in the success response body. Specify that display_title is present only in create/update responses. Do NOT add display_title to list or detail response schemas.

   1) Validation on incoming requests:
      - Add a request validation rule: if the request payload (JSON body) contains a top-level display_title key (or within the resource envelope where attributes are provided), return HTTP 422 with a clear error object.    2) Persistence and compute:
      - Continue to persist the full incoming "title" exactly as received into the canonical storage (DB). Do not mutate stored title to a truncated value.  
      - For create and update responses only, compute display_title using the explicit algorithm: measure the title string length by Unicode code points.    3) Response envelope:
      - Include display_title in the create/update success response body in the same envelope where the resource is returned. If your API uses resource/attributes nesting, include display_title there. Keep the field optional (present only on create/update responses).

Ensure the log-level and destination conform to existing logging policies. The contract requires that these server-side logs be retained (preserve existing retention policies); do not change retention policy, but ensure the new log entry is generated and included in the same logging pipeline.
